english: When I come, we will talk.
tip: After когда (kogda = when) about the future, Russian uses the future tense: приду (pridu = I will come), not present.

target: До тех пор пока не будет ответа, мы ждём.
english: Until we get an answer, we will wait.
tip: Negated быть (byt) takes the genitive: не будет ответа (ne budet otveta = there will be no answer), ответ (otvet) shifting to ответа.

target: Сломанный велосипед был починен моим отцом менее чем за час.
english: The broken bicycle was fixed by my father in less than an hour.
tip: In a passive, the doer goes in the instrumental: починен моим отцом (pochinen moim ottsom = fixed by my father).

english: Thanks to you everything worked out.
tip: благодаря (blagodarya = thanks to) takes the dative, not the genitive: благодаря тебе (... tebe = thanks to you).

english: He took the keys from the table.
tip: с, со (s, so = off a surface) takes the genitive: стол (stol) becomes со стола (so stola = off the table).

english: According to the plan, we will start tomorrow.
tip: согласно (soglasno = according to) takes the dative: согласно плану (... planu = according to the plan).

target: В отличие от брата, она тихая.
english: Unlike her brother, she is quiet.
tip: в отличие от (v otlichie ot = unlike) takes the genitive: в отличие от брата (... ot brata = unlike the brother).

target: Если ты придёшь, я буду рад.
english: If you come, I will be glad.
tip: если (esli = if) marks a real condition; don't confuse it with ли (li = whether) for indirect questions, as in придёт ли он (pridyot li on = whether he'll come).

english: The painting hangs above the couch.
tip: над (nad = above) takes the instrumental: над диваном (nad divanom = above the couch).

english: It's boring without you.
tip: без (bez = without) always takes the genitive, so ты (ty = you) becomes тебя (tebya = you).

english: The cat is under the table.
tip: For location, под (pod = under) takes the instrumental, so стол (stol = table) becomes столом (stolom = table).

english: She misses home.
tip: скучать по (skuchat po = to miss) takes the dative, so дом (dom = home) becomes дому (domu = home).

english: Before bed I read.
tip: перед (pered = before) takes the instrumental, so сон (son = sleep) becomes сном (snom = sleep).

english: We walked through the park.
tip: через (cherez = through) always takes the accusative: через парк (cherez park = through the park).

english: She hid behind a tree.
tip: For location, за (za = behind) takes the instrumental, so дерево (derevo = tree) becomes деревом (derevom = tree).

english: He walks around the park.
tip: For moving about a place, по (po = around) takes the dative: по парку (po parku = around the park).

english: I am sitting by the window.
tip: у (u = by) means right beside something and takes the genitive: у окна (u okna = by the window).

english: I will come in an hour.
tip: через (cherez = in) plus a time span means after that time: через час (cherez chas = in an hour).

english: During the day he worked.
tip: в течение (v techenie = during) takes the genitive, so день (den = day) becomes дня (dnya = day).

english: They always help each other.
tip: In друг другу (drug drugu = each other) only the second word declines, dative here after помогают (pomogayut = help).

english: Three years ago we met.
tip: Numbers 2 to 4 force genitive singular on the noun: три года (tri goda = three years).

english: They said that they don't know.
tip: In reported speech the tense does not shift back: знают (znayut = know) stays present after past сказали (skazali = said).

english: After saying goodbye to our friends, we left.
tip: Попрощавшись (Poproshchavshis = having said goodbye) is a perfective gerund: the action finishes before the main verb.

english: He pulled the box from under the bed.
tip: из-под (iz-pod = from under) is a single preposition taking the genitive: из-под кровати (iz-pod krovati = from under the bed).

target: Он работает с девяти до пяти.
english: He works from nine to five.
tip: For a range, с (s = from) and до (do = until) both take the genitive: с девяти до пяти (s devyati do pyati = from nine to five).

target: Мама велела, чтобы я убрал комнату.
english: Mom told me to clean the room.
tip: After ordering or wishing, чтобы (chtoby = that) takes a past-tense verb: чтобы я убрал (chtoby ya ubral = that I clean up).

target: Как пройти до ближайшей станции метро?
english: How do I get to the nearest metro station?
tip: Borrowed words like метро (metro = metro) never change form, staying метро (metro) in every case.

target: Почему ты не ответил на моё сообщение?
english: Why didn't you answer my message?
tip: The verb ответить (otvetit = answer) needs на (na = to) plus accusative: ответил на сообщение (otvetil na soobshchenie = answered the message).

target: На прошлой неделе мы были в театре.
english: Last week we were at the theater.
tip: Weeks take на (na = in), not в (v): на прошлой неделе (na proshloy nedele = last week), prepositional case.

target: Говоря по телефону, она ходила по комнате.
english: While talking on the phone, she walked around the room.
tip: Говоря (Govorya = while talking) is an imperfective gerund: it happens at the same time as ходила (khodila = was walking).
